traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 243 Verbenaceae: woody or herbaceous, the twigs often square; leaves usually opposite or whorled; no stipules; flowers more or less irregular; calyx 4- or 5-lobed, persisting; corolla united, a tube of 4 or 5 lobes; stamens 4, rarely 2 or 5; ovary superior; fruit a drupe or berry. APG moves Vitex, Callicarpa, teak, Clerodendrum and Premna to Lamiaceae; what stays (Verbena, Lantana, Lippia, Duranta, Petrea) has simple, often toothed or lobed leaves and a drupe or a fruit splitting in nutlets (Verbena's, inferred, not traced), so the division is left unstated. The order (Lamiales) states the stipules, the ovary and the two carpels.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Verbenaceae with Avicenniaceae, Dicrastylidaceae, Phrymataceae, Stilbaceae, Symphoremataceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Lucid family key, Verbenaceae (read 2026-10-17): outlines from linear to lanceolate, ovate, elliptic, oblanceolate, oblong, orbicular. Ranking ours, weighted by Verbena, Lippia, Lantana, Citharexylum, Stachytarpheta (largest genera in the narrow family), mostly ovate to elliptic.
